text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Cardiac assessment first: twelve-lead ECG today; a structured estimate of the chance of coronary disease; no troponin, because the pain is chronic and there is no acute episode; CT coronary angiography within a week, chosen over stress testing because it excludes both obstructive and non-obstructive plaque and informs the cholesterol decision; call 911 for chest pain at rest lasting more than a few minutes, or pain with breathlessness, sweating or fainting
  • Gastroenterology consultation for upper endoscopy within one week, with gastric biopsies for Helicobacter pylori, to find the cause of the chest and epigastric pain after the cardiac assessment and to advise on treatment; no acid-suppressing drug before the endoscopy, with an antacid as needed
  • Respectful review of the opium-containing remedy: what it is, why he takes it, and what it does for him; a DSM-5-TR assessment; a prescription drug monitoring program check; a urine drug test with his consent, explained as part of care; naloxone at home; no alcohol, sleep medicines or other sedatives on the same night; never more than his usual amount; stored closed and out of reach; how opioids slow the gut; no forced or abrupt taper, and any reduction his own choice, made slowly; reviewed at every visit, with the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
  • Chronic insomnia: cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) with the clinic's behavioral sleep clinician, six sessions, with a sleep diary, sleep restriction, stimulus control and work on racing thoughts at night; Insomnia Severity Index at intake and at each review; no hypnotic or sedating antihistamine, which would add to the opioid
  • Strain of command and mood: PHQ-9 and GAD-7 at intake and at follow-up; protected time for meals and sleep, decisions delegated after a set hour, and his evening writing kept; counselling if scores rise
  • Constipation: polyethylene glycol as needed, fluids and fiber; review as the remedy changes
  • Reflux esophagitis: omeprazole 20 mg 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast for eight weeks, then a trial off with omeprazole on demand; the evening meal at least three hours before lying down, the head of the bed raised, and less wine at night; no repeat endoscopy for grade B esophagitis; esophageal manometry and reflux monitoring off therapy if symptoms persist or swallowing becomes difficult
  • Mild COVID-19: rest, fluids and acetaminophen; honey for cough; no codeine or dextromethorphan cough medicine, sedating antihistamine or sleep aid while he takes the opium-containing remedy, and no more of the remedy than usual; naloxone at hand; antiviral treatment offered and declined after a shared decision; stay away from others until fever-free for 24 hours without medicine and improving, then added precautions for five days; call 911 for breathlessness, chest pain, confusion or blue lips, and return for oxygen saturation below 94% on a home oximeter
  • Colorectal cancer screening: colonoscopy ordered for the first quiet stretch of his assignment, with a split-dose bowel preparation and two extra days of polyethylene glycol beforehand because the opioid slows the bowel, and no remedy the night before; fecal immunochemical testing each year if he prefers not to have colonoscopy

resource.title: Marcus Aurelius synthetic care plan
resource.description: Evaluate chronic epigastric and lower chest pain after meals, with poor appetite and poor sleep, in a 53-year-old man who leads a large organization through a long field assignment, as current guidance advises: exclude a cardiac cause first (an ECG, a structured estimate of the chance of coronary disease, no troponin for chronic pain without an acute episode, and CT coronary angiography chosen by risk); then upper endoscopy with gastric biopsies for Helicobacter pylori, because chest pain without heartburn after a cardiac evaluation calls for objective testing for reflux; reach a diagnosis of erosive reflux esophagitis and say why peptic ulcer and functional dyspepsia were set aside; treat with an eight-week course of a proton pump inhibitor, timed meals and head-of-bed elevation, then step down to on-demand use; review, with respect and without judgment, an unregulated opium-containing herbal remedy he has taken for years (a DSM-5-TR assessment, a drug-monitoring check, a urine drug test with consent, naloxone, no sedatives or alcohol with it, and no forced taper, as the CDC 170 guideline advises), and recognize how opioids slow the gut; treat chronic insomnia with cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia rather than hypnotics; and attend to the strain of command. The modern episode is a teaching case, not a claim about the cause of his real complaints, and it does not attribute opioid addiction to him.
